# Report fixtures

Six Gauge JSON reports the renderer and the issue syncer are tested against. No test in
this repository touches the network, so these files are the record of what a real run
looks like.

Four of the six were produced by a real run on **testnet** on 2026-11-03 (UTC), which is
this organization's verification policy: Gauge is only ever run against testnet for its
own checks. They were generated by building `stellar-gauge` from `posture-sec/guage` at
`da656733fff839d5cf20f795460f4365a7254257` (`stellar-gauge 0.1.0-dev`) and running:

```bash
stellar-gauge check --network testnet --endpoint https://horizon-testnet.stellar.org \
  --format json GBQHXYDEJD6NEIUQ5NYDBVNTRCACJXMLO32JUQHBGO524NMVYOMIN5CP
stellar-gauge audit --config policy.toml --format json [--fail-on warn]
```

| File | Origin | What it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report-clean.json` | real run, ledger 5535684, exit 0 | the no-findings path: an empty list, `check` mode with one account |
| `report-findings.json` | real run, ledger 5535642, exit 1 | two accounts, one with `missing: true` and one `acct-missing` HIGH finding at fingerprint `b03faa6106f2405560196e0cad9e0bb74cab9c08d798877c0d795019bddd43d6` |
| `report-warn.json` | real run, ledger 5535646, exit 1 | a `warn` finding (`flag-undeclared-clawback`) at a `--fail-on warn` threshold |
| `report-network-mismatch.json` | real run, ledger 5535646, exit 1 | `skipped` as a string plus the `acct-network-mismatch` HIGH finding, the shape a policy that names one network and points at another produces |
| `report-accepted.json` | derived from `report-findings.json` | the `accepted: true` path, which no real run produced yet because no policy with an `[[accept]]` entry has been run |
| `report-hostile-strings.json` | derived from `report-clean.json` | markup and mentions inside chain-derived fields, which no real account has been observed to carry |

The two derived files are **hand-built**. Each is a copy of a captured report with these
changes and nothing else:

- `report-accepted.json`: `accepted` set to `true` on the one finding in
  `report-findings.json`. The fingerprint, account and message are the captured ones.
- `report-hostile-strings.json`: a `flag-drift` finding added with fingerprint `0`*64, its
  `evidence` carrying a markdown link and `@all`, the snapshot's `home_domain` set to
  `[click here](javascript:alert(1)) @all @somebody #hidden`, and `exit_code` moved to 1 so
  the report is consistent with the finding it now contains.

Both are labeled hand-built here and in the tests that read them, per the rule that a
fixture's provenance is written down. The markup in `report-hostile-strings.json` is
plausible rather than observed: `home_domain` is a string the account holder chooses and
Horizon serves it back unchanged, so it is the field a hostile value would arrive in.
Whether a real account on testnet or mainnet actually carries such a value has not been
checked, and no test here claims it has.

## Perishability

These are reports, not ledger reads, so a testnet reset cannot make a test fail: the files
are the record. The `tool_version` in all six is `0.1.0-dev`, which is what an unbuilt
release string looks like. When Gauge is tagged and this Action starts pinning a release,
the fixtures regenerate and this table's ledger numbers move with them.
